address: Meeuwenlaan 132, Amsterdam-Noord (Van der Pekbuurt): 1936 school complex (Breders Beroepscollege), yellow-grey brick wings of two and three storeys with white-framed bar windows under hipped blue-tile roofs with dormers, and a low translucent-clad wing carrying giant grey letters
notes: Meeuwenlaan 132 (BAG pand 0363100012101771, built 1936, 220 3DBAG wall surfaces, roof max 27.5 m): a 1930s school complex of the Van der Pekbuurt, today the Breders Beroepscollege (a banner on the site says so), about 100 m by 90 m round courtyards. Photographed: the 68 m north front (w01-3 2024: two storeys of white-framed bar windows in yellow-grey brick under a hipped dark-tile roof with seven dormers over a dark plinth), the east wing end (w07-93: red entrance door, 2 storeys), the west brick wing (w05-280: three storeys under a hipped slate roof), and the low translucent-clad wing on the west and south sides (w04-286, w03-168) carrying giant grey letters (BREDER... on the west, ...LEGE on the south). w02-183 and w06-78 have no panorama.

walls[0] = panel 157 (N, 68 m, eaves 9.6; surface 198): 2 storeys x 17 bays of wide bar windows. walls[1] = panel 79 (E, 24 m, eaves 9.7; surfaces 88, 106): 2 storeys x 6 bays. walls[2] = panels 122, 5, 7 (W, 8 m each, eaves 13.8; surfaces 147, 7, 9): 3 storeys x 6 bays. walls[3] = panel 121 (W low wing, 34 m, eaves 5.3; surface 146): glazed ground under a translucent upper band with the letters BREDERS on a cornice band (the photograph cuts the word at BREDER; the S comes from the Breders banner). walls[4] = panel 110 (S low wing, 43 m, eaves 6.6; surface 133): the same wing with COLLEGE, inferred from the visible ...LEGE ending in a blank panel. Simplified: the real letters are about 3 m tall and run straight across the translucent panels, here a cornice-band lettering; dormers, chimneys and the hipped roofs are the 3DBAG roof; the red entrance doors and the school banner are not modelled. Not drawn: the south and east courtyard fronts, the tower block (22.9 m) and the gym (no panorama), which stay blank brick.
